kicker: Apparel retail · like-for-like vs total sales growth, Q2 FY27
title: New stores, not old ones, carried apparel retail's Q2
dek: At all 7 chains, revenue grew faster than like-for-like sales (LFL: sales at stores open a year or more), by a median 8.3 points; October festivals hit old stores. Trent leaves the Sensex on 21 Dec.

chart.title: Sales growth, Q2 FY27 vs Q2 FY26
chart.sub: LFL as stated on Q2 calls · total revenue from filed results · sorted by gap

legend.b: Like-for-like (stores open a year or more)

read: The festival shift explains part of the gap, so Q3 LFL is the cleaner test of whether the old stores are still growing beneath the fast store roll-outs.
sources: Vantage analysis of Q2 FY27 results filed on BSE and Q2 FY27 earnings calls; Sensex change: Kotak Neo, 20 Nov 2026
notes: Like-for-like (LFL) or same-store sales growth is as each company stated it on its Q2 FY27 call (Vishal, V-Mart and V2 call it SSSG; ABLBL and Arvind give retail LFL only, which excludes wholesale and online); total revenue growth is year on year from the filed Q2 FY27 results (consolidated, except V-Mart, Vedant and Sai Silks standalone). The gap between the two is a rough measure of growth from stores opened in the last year, plus non-store channels at the brand companies. Festivals moved from September last year to October this year (Oct 11 vs Sep 22 last year for Navratri, per V-Mart), which depressed Q2 LFL: V-Mart put festival-adjusted LFL at 11% against 3% reported, Vishal at about 9% against 5.4%, and Arvind at about 10% against 7.3%. V2 Retail opened 106 stores in H1 and said FY28 openings could fall to about 100 from 150–200 if Q3 stays weak. Store openings in Q2: Vishal 26 gross, V2 Retail 49, ABLBL over 100; V2's new stores sell 35–40% less per square foot than mature ones. News hook: Shriram Finance replaces Trent in the Sensex from 21 Dec (Kotak Neo, 20 Nov 2026); Trent's filed Q2 revenue rose 21.9% but it has no Q2 call summary with an LFL figure, so it is not charted. Also left out: Shoppers Stop (no call summary), Go Fashion (LFL described only as 'broadly flat'), Credo Brands (inconsistent Q2 figures on the call), ABFRL/Pantaloons and Raymond Lifestyle (festival-adjusted or non-numeric LFL only), SS Retail (no comparable filed revenue growth) and footwear makers that gave no LFL figure.
